Launch tags:SaaS•Developer Tools•Artificial Intelligence [...] That's what we built Yedric to do. Yedric is an embeddable AI agent that turns what your app can already do into things users can simply ask for. You give Yedric access to your product knowledge, user context, and APIs, and he can actually get things done inside your app.

We originally built this technology for our own Shopify apps. We wanted users to be able to say things like "turn off email notifications" or "fix my broken integration" and have the app handle it for them instead of sending them through docs, support, or a maze of settings.

Then something unexpected happened. [...] One example I like is combining data from multiple read operations. Instead of exporting everything to Excel and manually putting it together, you can just ask for the result you want directly in the app.

@samir\_asadov This is a good one! I definitely see merchants entering more sophisticated prompts as they continue to use our AI Assistant, Yedric.

MESA has a growing library of pre-built templates that the AI assistant can pull in when a merchant’s goal aligns with their use case. Yedric is designed to guide that process by asking a few clarifying questions and helping shape the workflow based on what the merchant is trying to accomplish.

What we typically see is merchants start with a generated or templated workflow, then refine and reuse those builds over time as they get more familiar with what works for their business. From there, everything is customizable. Templates can be adjusted, extended, or rebuilt with AI as needed. [...] All of the pre-built templates are viewable here: 

Report

Samir Asadov

@shannon\_torchia  That's the right model — templated start, then refine through use is exactly how non-developer users actually internalize automation patterns. The same dynamic shows up in financial-modeling teaching: students who start from a working model and break/rebuild parts of it learn faster than those who start from a blank workbook. The Yedric clarifying-questions flow is what's missing from most generative tools — they jump to a build before establishing the constraints. Looking forward to seeing how the template library evolves; once it crosses the long-tail threshold, the AI assistant becomes mostly a router, which is the cheap-to-run end-state.

Report

Priya K [...] If you need deeper help, you can use our AI assistant, Yedric, to investigate the workflow, explain the error, and even help you update the automation logic. Once changes are made, you can run workflow tests to verify the fix before putting it back into production.

For merchants that expect intermittent third-party outages, MESA also supports building fallback and error-handling logic directly into workflows. For example, you can retry tasks, route around failures, notify teams, or temporarily queue work elsewhere when an integration is unavailable.

Finally, if a downstream system was unavailable for a period of time, you can use our Time Travel feature to replay historical events and recover missed automations after the issue is resolved.
